title: Publish (internal) Arcadia Health customer story draft — Private deployment
author: Ben Carter
commits: docs(stories): add Arcadia Health private deployment draft page (internal-only)
docs(nav): add gated Customer stories entry + noindex handling for internal pages
docs(components): add InternalOnlyBanner + approval checklist callout
chore: fix link-check failures and image alt text
description:
Summary: Adds an Arcadia Health customer story draft page to the docs site for internal review + enablement (Sales/CS/SE), with explicit gating and a prominent “NOT PUBLIC / NEEDS CUSTOMER APPROVAL” banner. This is intended to support the Customer Reference Program workstream (PM-684) while Legal/Security approvals and metrics validation are still in progress.

Context: Arcadia Health is a regulated workload evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) and has strict constraints on what can be published (no sensitive architecture details, no named sub-processors, no exact retention windows, no screenshots with account identifiers). This PR intentionally publishes an internal-only draft to unblock internal review and sales enablement, while we collect final approvals and validated metrics.

What’s included: (1) New MDX story page at /customer-stories/arcadia-health-private-deployment marked internal-only. (2) Internal-only banner at top of page with an approval checklist + owner pointers. (3) Gating logic so the page is only discoverable/rendered when INTERNAL_CONTENT=1 (or equivalent) is enabled in the docs build; otherwise it 404s and is excluded from nav/search. (4) “noindex” applied to internal pages; link checker ignores internal-only routes in public builds.

Customer story draft notes: The draft intentionally uses placeholders for metrics and carefully-scoped language: • Performance numbers are written as [TBD: validated p95 window + workload shape] • Reliability claims avoid absolute language and reference “observed during evaluation window” • Security language is high-level (VPC isolation, audit logs export support) and avoids naming internal controls beyond what’s already in our standard public security posture docs.

Approval checklist embedded on the page (must be completed before this goes public): 1) Customer quote + logo release executed (Commercial Counsel + GC). 2) Security/claims review (Naomi) confirms no sensitive implementation details, retention specifics, or audit log fields that could increase risk. 3) Metrics validation worksheet completed + owner sign-off (SE + telemetry) for latency/error rate claims and measurement window. 4) Customer final review + written approval via email for the exact quotes, company name usage, and architecture diagram.

Implementation details: • internalContent.ts introduces a single gate used by both nav generation and route rendering. • InternalOnlyBanner component is intentionally loud and repeats “Do not share externally.” • Added placeholder architecture diagram asset (genericized; does not reflect customer network specifics).

Testing/verification: - Local: yarn dev with INTERNAL_CONTENT=1 shows the page and nav; without it the page is not reachable. - CI: docs-build + lint + typecheck + link-check. Link-check initially failed due to a missing alt attribute and an internal route referenced from a public index; fixed by moving the internal index under the same gating and ensuring public index doesn’t link to internal routes.

CI checks: ✅ docs-build (Node 20) ✅ lint ✅ typecheck ✅ link-check ✅ spellcheck (customer-stories allowlist)

Review notes: - Soojin Lee (Product Marketing): requested tighter wording on outcomes; avoid “reduced incident rate” without incident taxonomy + window; added “observed during pilot window” qualifier and moved all quantified claims to a clearly labeled Metrics (TBD) block. - Naomi Feldman (Security/claims): flagged a sentence that implied specific log retention; removed exact retention wording and replaced with “configurable retention per customer policy.” Also requested removal of a bullet listing audit log field names; replaced with link to generic audit logging doc and a note that field-level details are available under NDA. - Markus Klein (SE): asked for clearer separation between Redwood product features vs Arcadia implementation choices; updated Architecture section to label “Redwood provided” vs “Customer-owned.” - Tessa Morgan (Design): requested consistent callout styling and a simpler diagram caption; added ApprovalChecklistCallout component and updated captioning.

Merge plan: Squash merge. This stays internal-only until approval checklist is fully complete. Follow-up PR will (a) remove internal gating for this page, (b) replace placeholders with validated metrics, (c) swap in customer-approved diagram and quotes, and (d) add to public Customer stories index + PDF.

Follow-ups: - PM-701: hook up intake form link and reference-request routing from this page (internal enablement section). - SUP-2381: audit log export format clarifications should be reflected in the security FAQ snippet once final.

Risk/mitigation: Primary risk is accidental public exposure via indexing or linking. Mitigations in this PR: noindex + gating at route and nav + internal builds only. Please do not paste content externally; the page includes explicit reminders.

Co-authored-by: Ethan Wallace (story draft content) / Simran Kaur (architecture review notes)
release_notes: Internal-only Arcadia Health Private deployment customer story draft page added for cross-functional review; includes gating + noindex and an embedded approval checklist for public release readiness.
